question_text: A piece of metal is subjected to a cyclic stress of 80 MPa. If the phase angle $\delta = 0.1^\circ$ and no heat is transferred to the surroundings, what will be the temperature rise after 100,000 cycles? Data: $E = 80 \text{ GPa}$, $C = 800 \text{ J} / (\text{kg} \cdot \text{K})$, and $\rho = 4.2 \text{ Mg} / \text{m}^3$.The unit of the answer is $ {}^{\circ} C$.
response:
## Solution

This is a **self-heating under cyclic stress** problem. The phase angle δ between stress and strain represents internal (viscoelastic) damping; the area of the stress–strain hysteresis loop is the energy dissipated as heat per unit volume per cycle.

**Energy dissipated per unit volume per cycle** (hysteresis loop area):

$$\Delta w = \pi\,\sigma_0 \varepsilon_0 \sin\delta = \pi\,\frac{\sigma_0^2}{E}\sin\delta$$

With no heat transferred to the surroundings, all dissipated energy raises the temperature:

$$N\,\Delta w = \rho\,C\,\Delta T \;\;\Longrightarrow\;\; \Delta T = \frac{N\,\pi\,\sigma_0^2\,\sin\delta}{E\,\rho\,C}$$

**Unit-faithful conversions** (per the unit-conversion skill):
- $\sigma_0 = 80\ \text{MPa} = 8.0\times10^{7}\ \text{Pa}$
- $E = 80\ \text{GPa} = 8.0\times10^{10}\ \text{Pa}$
- $\rho = 4.2\ \text{Mg/m}^3 = 4.2\times10^{3}\ \text{kg/m}^3$
- $\delta = 0.1^\circ = 1.7453\times10^{-3}\ \text{rad}$
- $C = 800\ \text{J/(kg·K)}$, $N = 10^{5}$

**Computation:**

$$\Delta T = \frac{(10^{5})\,\pi\,(8.0\times10^{7})^{2}\,\sin(0.1^\circ)}{(8.0\times10^{10})(4.2\times10^{3})(800)}$$

The arithmetic gives $\Delta w \approx 438.6\ \text{J/m}^3$ per cycle, total $4.386\times10^{7}\ \text{J/m}^3$, and

$$\Delta T = \frac{4.386\times10^{7}}{(4200)(800)} \approx 13.06\ ^\circ\text{C}$$

The dominant input precision is 2 significant figures (80 MPa, 80 GPa, 4.2 Mg/m³), so rounding to 2 sig figs:

$$\boxed{13}$$
